outcomes.description: Same data, no fault. Any difference is a false positive.
outcomes.note: no false positives across all dates

outcomes.description: Post a 555.00 cash settlement INTO a closed business day. The books for that day now differ from what was reported at close; the replay must say so.
evidence: new history drift: nas.payment_summary.payment_count vs snapshot.payments.payment_count, nas.payment_summary.total_collected vs snapshot.payments.total_collected, nas.payment_summary.total_collected vs stored.total_revenue
outcomes.note: 1 row(s) changed; every declared effect occurred

outcomes.description: Move a single closed-day payment by ONE PAISA. The framework claims no tolerance band on history; this is the test of that claim. A rounding-tolerant replay would let a systematic sub-rupee drift through on every day at once.
evidence: new history drift: nas.payment_summary.total_collected vs snapshot.payments.total_collected, nas.payment_summary.total_collected vs stored.total_revenue
outcomes.note: 1 row(s) changed; every declared effect occurred

outcomes.description: Void a payment that belongs to a closed day. Voiding after the close removes money from a period that has already been reported and reconciled.
evidence: new history drift: nas.payment_summary.payment_count vs snapshot.payments.payment_count, nas.payment_summary.total_collected vs snapshot.payments.total_collected, nas.payment_summary.total_collected vs stored.total_revenue
outcomes.note: 1 row(s) changed; every declared effect occurred

outcomes.description: Post a 222.00 charge into the closed day. Accrual revenue for a reported period must not be able to change without the replay noticing.
evidence: new history drift: nas.revenue_summary.accrual_net vs snapshot.revenue.accrual_net, nas.revenue_summary.accrual_net vs stored.accrual_revenue
outcomes.note: 1 row(s) changed; every declared effect occurred

outcomes.description: Raise the priced rate of one room night that belongs to the closed day by 111.00. The nightly rate record is the closest thing the schema has to an immutable statement of what a room was sold for.
outcomes.note: 1 row(s) changed; every declared effect occurred

outcomes.description: Rewrite the stored close total for the audited day. The night audit log is the hotel's own statement about the day; altering it must not be quiet.
evidence: new history drift: nas.payment_summary.total_collected vs stored.total_revenue
outcomes.note: 1 row(s) changed; every declared effect occurred

outcomes.description: Tamper with the frozen snapshot without touching its hash. The application claims a tamper-detection control here; this proves the claim, and proves the replay surfaces it.
outcomes.note: 1 row(s) changed; every declared effect occurred

outcomes.description: Post a 444.00 payment on the closed day through a mode whose category is neither direct_payment nor ota_receivable. The night audit buckets anything that is not OTA as direct cash; kpi_helpers requires the category to be direct_payment exactly. The two therefore disagree, and the ledger — which counts it as neither — is what reveals which of them moved.

Remove the one declared as-at exclusion and require the drift it was masking to be reported. This is the proof that PASS A and PASS C really ran under different clocks and that the comparator compares them.
outcomes.note: 27 past date(s) reported drift on 1 path(s) once unmasked

outcomes.description: Stored replay compared against itself.
The primary record for the closed day 2026-05-27 moved by one paisa.
The application now reports a different cash figure for the closed day 2026-05-27.
The frozen close for 2026-05-27 was rewritten.
The snapshot integrity verdict for 2026-05-27 changed.
2026-05-27 was reopened after being closed.
2026-05-27 is missing from the stored replay — a day of trading that no longer exists.
A date appears that is earlier than any the stored replay knows about — a posting back-dated into a period that did not exist.
A reconciliation that held on 2026-05-27 now fails.
A figure on 2026-05-27 became dependent on the order the dates were replayed in.
The CURRENT business date 2026-05-28 took 5,000 more in cash. The hotel is trading; this must be reported and must NOT block. A gate that fails every day is a gate that gets switched off.
